newsitem.title: UK: Daiwa overweights Polish stocks, sees 1997 rally.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa overweights Polish stocks, sees 1997 rally.

text.p: The Polish stock market is likely to hover around current levels until the end of the year but with good fundamentals and new listings, 1997 is looking good, Daiwa Europe said in a research report.
"Despite the recent market jitters, we remain optimistic that there are still gains to be made, although the market is likely to move sideways until 1997," Daiwa strategist Sonja Shechter said.
She noted that a selloff in first line stocks with the WIG index of leading shares down at under 13,600 points from a year high of 15,078 had not been matched in the second tier market.

"This is partly due to the fact that domestic investors make up the largest portion of investors and own approximately 40 percent of the capitalisation on the main market and nearly 70 percent on the parallel market," Schechter research said.
Daiwa says that a surge in domestic consumption is set to continue, and picks furniture maker Forte, and food processors, Drosed and Sokolow.
"The domestic economy remains strong with domestic demand increasing dramatically, as evidenced by the 64 percent increase in consumer credit from January to September," Shechter said.
It notes that the construction sector is moving out of the doldrums but says that stock-picking is essential in this sector.
"We recommend Mostostal Warszawa and Mostostal Zabrze," Shechter said.
In the banking sector, Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA is Daiwa's favoured stock.
